question:
Red Bean Clothing Factory uses three specialized machines to produce shirts, short-sleeved shirts, and casual wear. The labor, material, selling price, and variable cost per unit for the three products are given in Table 5-10.
Table 5-10
\begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c}
\hline Product Name & Labor per unit & Material per unit & Selling Price & Variable Cost \
\hline Shirt & 3 & 4 & 120 & 60 \
\hline Short-sleeved shirt & 2 & 3 & 80 & 40 \
\hline Casual wear & 6 & 6 & 180 & 80 \
\hline
\end{tabular}

It is known that the factory has a weekly labor capacity of 150 units and a material capacity of 160 units. The fixed costs per week for producing shirts, short-sleeved shirts, and casual wear with the specialized machines are 2000, 1500, and 1000, respectively. Design a weekly production plan for the factory to maximize profit.

"""
Red Bean Clothing Factory - weekly profit-maximizing production plan.

Decision variables
==================
  x[p] : units produced per week of product p, p in P
         -> model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
  y[p] : 1 if product p's specialized machine is used that week, else 0
         -> model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

Objective (maximize)
====================
  max  sum_p (price[p] - vcost[p]) * x[p]  -  sum_p fixed[p] * y[p]

Constraints by source sentence
=============================
  C1 (prose: weekly labor capacity of 150 units)
        sum_p labor[p] * x[p] <= labor_cap
  C2 (prose: weekly material capacity of 160 units)
        sum_p material[p] * x[p] <= material_cap
  C3 (prose: fixed cost per week incurred for producing each product
      with its specialized machine)
        x[p] <= M[p] * y[p]   for all p in P
  (domains: production quantities nonnegative integers; machine-use y in {0,1})

Data
====
All numeric constants are stored in DATA and referenced only through DATA.
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "products": ["shirt", "short_sleeve", "casual"],
    "labor": {"shirt": 3, "short_sleeve": 2, "casual": 6},
    "material": {"shirt": 4, "short_sleeve": 3, "casual": 6},
    "price": {"shirt": 120, "short_sleeve": 80, "casual": 180},
    "vcost": {"shirt": 60, "short_sleeve": 40, "casual": 80},
    "fixed": {"shirt": 2000, "short_sleeve": 1500, "casual": 1000},
    "labor_cap": 150,
    "material_cap": 160,
    # Big-M per product: an upper bound on production implied by resources.
    "bigM": {"shirt": 150, "short_sleeve": 150, "casual": 150},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(
            (d["price"][p] - d["vcost"][p]) * m.x[p] - d["fixed"][p] * m.y[p]
            for p in m.P
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    def labor_rule(m):
        return sum(d["labor"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["labor_cap"]

    model.labor_cap_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

    def material_rule(m):
        return sum(d["material"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["material_cap"]

    model.material_cap_con = pyo.Constraint(rule=material_rule)

    def link_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["bigM"][p] * m.y[p]

    model.link_con = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=link_rule)

    return model

    # Labor per unit for each product
    "labor_per_unit": {1: 3, 2: 2, 3: 6},

    # Selling price per unit

    # Variable cost per unit
    "var_cost": {1: 60, 2: 40, 3: 80},
    # Fixed weekly costs for using each specialized machine
    "fixed_cost": {1: 2000, 2: 1500, 3: 1000},
    # Weekly resource capacities
    "labor_capacity": 150,
    "material_capacity": 160,
    # Big-M per product: max units producible under both resource limits
    "big_m": {1: 37, 2: 53, 3: 25},
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])

    # --- Variables ---
    # Units produced of each product (integer, nonnegative)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, None))
    # Binary indicator: fixed cost / machine used for product p
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # --- Objective: maximize profit = sum(contribution margin * units) - fixed costs ---
    def obj_rule(m):
        margin = sum((d["price"][p] - d["var_cost"][p]) * m.x[p] for p in m.P)
        fixed = sum(d["fixed_cost"][p] * m.y[p] for p in m.P)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # --- Constraints ---

    # Labor capacity: sum(labor_p * x_p) <= labor_capacity
    def labor_rule(m):
        return sum(d["labor_per_unit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["labor_capacity"]

    model.labor_cap = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

    # Material capacity: sum(material_p * x_p) <= material_capacity

        return sum(d["material_per_unit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["material_capacity"]

    model.material_cap = pyo.Constraint(rule=material_rule)

    # Fixed-cost activation: x_p <= big_m_p * y_p  (produce only if machine used)
    def activation_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["big_m"][p] * m.y[p]

    model.activation = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=activation_rule)

    return model

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"], ordered=True)
    m.R = pyo.Set(initialize=d["resources"], ordered=True)

    # Decision variables
    m.produce = pyo.Var(m.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    m.is_active = pyo.Var(m.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: maximize profit = contribution margin - fixed costs

            (d["selling_price"][p] - d["variable_cost"][p]) * m.produce[p]
            for p in m.P
        )

        return margin - fixed

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Resource capacity constraints (one per resource)
    def capacity_rule(m, r):
        return sum(d["usage"][p][r] * m.produce[p] for p in m.P) <= d["capacity"][r]

#   y[p] : binary, 1 if the specialized machine for product p is used

#     sum_p (unit contribution margin * x[p]) - sum_p (fixed cost * y[p])

#   C3. Fixed-cost activation: x[p] <= big_m * y[p]  for all p
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    "products": ["shirt", "short_shirt", "casual_wear"],
    "labor_per_unit": {"shirt": 3, "short_shirt": 2, "casual_wear": 6},

    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    def contribution(p):
        return d["selling_price"][p] - d["variable_cost"][p]

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(contribution(p) * m.x[p] for p in m.P) - sum(
            d["fixed_cost"][p] * m.y[p] for p in m.P
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    def labor_rule(m):
        return sum(d["labor_per_unit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["labor_capacity"]

    model.labor_capacity = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

    def material_rule(m):
        return (
            sum(d["material_per_unit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)
            <= d["material_capacity"]
        )

    model.material_capacity = pyo.Constraint(rule=material_rule)

    def activation_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["big_m"] * m.y[p]

    model.activation = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=activation_rule)

    return model

    # Per-unit contribution margin = Selling Price - Variable Cost
    margin = {
        p: d["selling_price"][p] - d["variable_cost"][p] for p in products
    }

    # Big-M upper bound per product: the largest quantity the two shared
    # resources could ever allow (linear, constant data only).
    big_m = {}
    for p in products:
        by_labor = d["labor_capacity"] // d["labor_per_unit"][p]
        by_material = d["material_capacity"] // d["material_per_unit"][p]
        big_m[p] = min(by_labor, by_material)

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=products)

    # ---- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    # x[p]: weekly production quantity of product p (integer units)
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.P,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=lambda m, p: (0, big_m[p]),
    )
    # y[p]: 1 if product p is produced this week (incurs its fixed cost), else 0
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # ---- Objective: maximize weekly profit --------------------------------
    # profit = sum_p (margin_p * x_p) - sum_p (fixed_p * y_p)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(margin[p] * model.x[p] for p in model.P)
        - sum(d["fixed_cost"][p] * model.y[p] for p in model.P),
        sense=pyo.maximize,
    )

    # ---- Constraints ------------------------------------------------------
    # Labor capacity: sum_p labor_p * x_p <= 150
    def labor_rule(m):
        return sum(d["labor_per_unit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["labor_capacity"]

    model.labor_capacity = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

    # Material capacity: sum_p material_p * x_p <= 160
    def material_rule(m):
        return sum(d["material_per_unit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["material_capacity"]

    model.material_capacity = pyo.Constraint(rule=material_rule)

    # Fixed-cost activation: x_p <= M_p * y_p  (charge fixed cost if produced)
    def activate_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= big_m[p] * m.y[p]

    model.activate_fixed = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=activate_rule)

    return model
